note: Buyer profiles as data. Guidance and rules of thumb, not advice. Policy numbers live in policy-tables.json, never here. 'heuristic' entries are agent rules of thumb, not regulations.

new_launch_condo.label: New-launch condominium

ccr.label: Core Central Region (prime districts 9, 10, 11 and the downtown core)
ccr.fit: Capital-preservation and expat/HNW demand; high entry price and ABSD exposure make it a poor first-home choice.
ccr.tradeoff: Highest psf and holding cost; resale depth tied to wealthy and foreign demand.

rcr.label: Rest of Central Region (city-fringe)
rcr.fit: Short commutes and strong rental demand; smaller units common.
rcr.tradeoff: Pricey per sq ft; compact layouts; more en-bloc and investor churn.

ocr.label: Outside Central Region (suburban)
ocr.fit: Best space per dollar for families; strong school/amenity catchments near regional hubs.
ocr.tradeoff: Longer commute; pick near an MRT interchange or a regional centre.

tradeoffs: Progressive payments: only 5% booking + 15% at S&P up front, then stage payments, so cash needs are spread over the build; but you may pay rent or an existing mortgage during the 3-5 year wait.
Developer sale price carries a new-launch premium over comparable resale; check against nearby resale psf with --mode private.
Fringe vs suburban: fringe buys commute and rental depth; suburban buys space and school options. Match to the profile's priority.

resale_condo.label: Resale condominium
tradeoffs: Lease: 99-year leasehold loses bank-loan and resale appeal as the remaining lease shortens; freehold or 999-year holds value better but costs more upfront.
Age: buildings over ~20-25 years may face major repairs, special levies and en-bloc speculation; check the sinking fund and MCST minutes.
Size and unit mix: a project of mostly small units skews to investor/tenant residents and quick resale turnover; larger units suit owner-occupiers.
Immediate possession and visible stock: you see the unit, view and neighbours before committing.

resale_hdb.label: Resale HDB flat

estates.mature: Established amenities, MRT, schools and higher resale prices; older lease commencement dates are common.
estates.non_mature: Newer leases and larger flats, often lower prices; amenities and transport may still be maturing.

tradeoffs: Remaining lease: below the age-95 coverage threshold, CPF usage and HDB loan amount are pro-rated (see policy-tables cpf_usage); very short leases may limit financing and future resale.
MOP: a resale flat must be occupied for the minimum occupation period before it can be sold on the open market; plan the next move accordingly.
3Gen flats: designed for multi-generation families and only resalable to eligible multi-generation families.
Income ceilings and grants apply to resale purchases (see policy-tables ehg / income_ceilings); household income can disqualify or reduce grants.

ec.label: Executive Condominium
tradeoffs: Condo facilities at a price below comparable private launches, with a minimum occupation period and eligibility income ceiling at first purchase.
MSR applies to EC loans during the MOP, which can bind harder than TDSR for mid-income couples.
Becomes fully private after the privatisation period; resale pool widens then.

dink.label: Dual-income couple, no kids (DINK)
priorities: Commute time and MRT interchange access for two workplaces
Resale liquidity and rental demand (flexibility to upgrade, downsize or rent out)
Low maintenance cost and a manageable monthly commitment (keep savings rate high)
Lifestyle: nearby dining and recreation over school catchment
Optionality: keep the lease and location sellable to the broadest buyer pool

shortlist.why: Compact 1-2 bedroom units near MRT with immediate possession; no wait and no progressive-interest overlap.
shortlist.watch_out: Avoid short remaining leases and very small projects with weak resale pools.

shortlist.why: Fringe or suburban launches near MRT give a fresh lease and facilities; progressive payments spread cash.
shortlist.watch_out: New-launch premium; carrying cost of rent during the build.

shortlist.why: Lowest total cost of occupancy; 4-room in a mature, MRT-served estate is liquid and cheap to hold.
shortlist.watch_out: Income ceiling for grants; MOP; consider lifestyle add-ons to approximate condo facilities.

shortlist.why: Only relevant if eligible and happy to wait out the MOP; DINK incomes can exceed the EC ceiling.

location.mrt: Walk to a station within ~5-10 min (heuristic); interchanges preferred; test both commutes at peak hour.
location.jobs: Weigh both workplaces; a city-fringe or interchange location usually wins.
location.amenities: Dining, gym, supermarket, park within walking distance; school catchment is secondary (but matters for resale to families).

key_questions: How many years do we plan to stay, and when might we upgrade or start a family?
What monthly commitment keeps our savings rate at target after the stress-tested instalment?
Does the lease and unit size appeal to the next buyer pool (families, investors, expats)?
red_flags: Remaining lease under ~60 years on a private leasehold with weak resale evidence
Stress-tested TDSR/MSR above the limit or barely passing
Project dominated by sub-500 sq ft units with high rental churn

first_home_couple.label: Couple buying their first home together
priorities: Affordability: lowest upfront cash and a monthly instalment that survives a rate rise and one income dropping
A home that fits children later (3 bedrooms or a large 4-room) and school catchment
Liquidity: avoid a lease or location that is hard to resell
Preserve cash and CPF buffer for renovation, furnishing and emergencies

shortlist.why: Grants (EHG, family grant) and HDB loan lower cash needs; best value if within the income ceilings.
shortlist.watch_out: Income ceiling for grants; lease remaining; MOP; price vs valuation (COV).

shortlist.why: Condo facilities at a lower price with a fresh lease; suited if eligible.
shortlist.watch_out: EC income ceiling; MSR; MOP; progressive payment cash schedule.

shortlist.why: Suburban resale condos can be cheaper than new launches and deliver immediate possession.
shortlist.watch_out: Cash down payment of at least 5% under bank loans; ageing project costs.

shortlist.why: Spread payments over the build; only if household income comfortably clears TDSR at the stress rate.
shortlist.watch_out: Double-housing cost during the wait; completion delays.

location.mrt: Within walking distance of a station on a line serving both workplaces.
location.jobs: Balance both commutes; avoid a long commute for one at the other's expense.
location.amenities: Supermarket, clinic, hawker/food, park; check the primary school catchment if kids are planned.

key_questions: Are we both first-timers and citizens/PRs, and what grants do we qualify for?
How much can we put in cash vs CPF, and what is the buffer after exercise and completion?
What happens to the instalment at the stress-test rate, and if one income stops for six months?
red_flags: Leaving less than a few months of expenses in cash after completion
Reliance on a grant the household income may not qualify for
Buying at an asking price well above the valuation without cash for the gap

family_of_five.label: Family of five (two parents, three children)
priorities: Space: enough bedrooms and bathrooms for five; 5-room HDB or a 3-4 bedroom condo
Primary-school access: distance bands to preferred schools
Total monthly commitment vs. income, including childcare, tuition and a car if needed
Safety and convenience: playground, park, clinic, childcare, supermarket within walking distance
Long-run lease: stay 15+ years without lease anxiety

shortlist.why: Large 5-room or executive flats in non-mature or mature estates give the most space per dollar; lowest cost of occupancy.
shortlist.watch_out: Lease remaining, floor/level, noise, distance to preferred schools, MOP.

shortlist.why: Three-bedroom EC with facilities if the household is eligible; good for growing families.
3-4 bedroom suburban resale condo: facilities for children, immediate possession.
shortlist.watch_out: Cash down payment, maintenance fees, ageing building, 99-year lease remaining.

shortlist.why: Larger suburban launches with fresh lease and facilities; only if cash flow supports the wait.
shortlist.watch_out: Wait of several years while paying existing housing cost; larger quantum is TDSR-sensitive.

location.mrt: Within ~10 min (heuristic) of a station; a bus interchange or feeder is acceptable for a family.

distance_bands.within_1km: Higher priority at primary-school registration for residents within 1 km
distance_bands.between_1_and_2km: Next band between 1 km and 2 km

schools.unverified_reason: MOE Primary 1 registration phases and distance bands were not fetched from moe.gov.sg in this review; confirm the current phase rules and the school's vacancies with MOE before buying.

location.jobs: Two workplaces plus school runs: favour mid-way or an interchange.
location.amenities: Playground, park, childcare, clinic, supermarket, enrichment centres.

key_questions: Which primary school do we want, and what is the walk or drive distance from this unit?
Does the unit have enough bedrooms for five now and as children grow older?
What is the total monthly commitment including childcare, tuition and transport?
red_flags: A unit that forces a long school run or an unsafe route
Monthly commitment that leaves little slack for childcare or tuition
Short remaining lease on a flat meant to be a 15-year home

multigen.label: Family of five with parents or grandparents in the household (multi-generation)
extra_priorities: Grandparent-friendly access: lift to the unit, step-free routes, nearby clinic and polyclinic
Separate bedroom and bathroom for elders; space to give everyone privacy
Proximity to one set of parents (Proximity Housing Grant) versus living together

shortlist_override.why: 3Gen flats and large resale flats are designed for extended families; lift/ramp access and clinics matter.
shortlist_override.watch_out: 3Gen flat resale restricted to eligible multi-generation families; extended-family income rules (see income_ceilings); check the HDB-eligibility of the parents.

shortlist_override.why: Large condo with a dual-key or study that can host elders.
shortlist_override.watch_out: Cost; MCST fees; ABSD if any household member already owns property.

red_flags: Elders owning residential property that triggers ABSD or disqualifies grants
Stairs or long walks to MRT/bus for older family members

related_skills.use: Check dengue cluster density and rainfall pressure for the town before committing.
Check current PSI/PM2.5 and haze exposure for the area.
Check commute and carpark options to workplaces.
Check rental yield if the unit may be rented out later.
Verify the property agent's CEA registration.
